//: LibreLane configuration. Base: the Tiny Tapeout CMOS5L template (Apache-2.0). Changes from the template are marked with a //<name> comment key next to them. See NOTICE.md for the origin of the memory-block settings.
//meta: Adds one step after the power-grid generator: it runs the tile's Metal4 power stripes across the memory block so the block is powered. The step is in librelane_plugin_jsasic_pdn.py and odb_stripes.py at the repository root.
//clock: 16.66 ns = 60 MHz, the project's target clock.
//pdn: Power stripes matched to the memory block's supply columns (11.24 um pitch, VDD and VSS 5.62 um apart). Width 2.1 + spacing 3.52 = 5.62; pitch 44.96 = 4 x 11.24; offset 6.15 puts the first VPWR stripe centre at x = 9.03, which is the first supply column of a block placed at x = 3.36. Template values were pitch 50.0, width 2.1.
//pdn_cfg: LibreLane's power-grid script without its per-block grid, which has no shapes on a single-layer grid and makes the generator fail. The block gets its power from Project.ExtendPowerStripes instead.
//stripes: Every-other mode: the tile grid's stripe pairs plus a pair on every other column pair of each bit-cell array.
//halo: Keeps standard cells away from the memory block's edge.
//drc: Magic reads the memory block from its abstract and reports the power stripes crossing it as overlaps. DRC is done by KLayout with the CMOS5L deck instead, which sees the real layout.
//macros: One IHP single-port 256 x 32 memory block (416.64 x 118.78 um) at the bottom left. Orientation FS puts its pin edge on top, facing the logic. Corner names are LibreLane's; the block's fast corner was characterized at -55 C.
//pdn_connect: Tells the power-grid tools that the block's VDD!, VDDARRAY! and VSS! pins are the tile's VPWR and VGND.
//obstructions: No signal routing across the memory block on any routing layer (the tile routes on Metal2 to Metal4 only). Rectangle = block footprint: x 3.36..420.0, y 3.78..122.56.
